current.text: He is a projected starter at forward next to De'Andre Hunter, with Acuff, LaVine and Sabonis in the starting group. Nobody is pushing that group for a starting spot.
Westbrook, Schroder and DeRozan have left the Kings. That frees shots and usage on the team.
Experts expect more usage and big minutes for him because the Kings cleared out usage.
He projects as about the third option on offense and will carry a heavy defensive load.
He is going too late in drafts. Josh is happy to take him in round 10 and expects about a top 100 season.
His ESPN rank of 83 is too high.
Experts doubt that his high block rate from last season will hold. They also doubt that his shooting returns.
If he reaches about 20 percent usage and shoots better, he can easily beat his draft spot.
He is 26 and in the first year of a 5-year, 140 million USD contract.
Ham says this is the season he has to prove himself.
His passes turned into assists at a low 46 percent rate last season because Kings teammates could not shoot.

durable.text: A finger injury early and an ankle injury late cost him most of the 2025-26 season.
In a small sample last season he blocked a lot of shots and defended well.
Ham says he has made big strides as a defender and rebounder.
The shooting from his rookie season has not come back.
He is a better category league player than points league player.

note: Murray is a late-round auction target at 1 to 3 USD. Yahoo values him at 2 USD and ESPN at 4 USD, and he went for 1 USD in our league last season. The experts see him as about a top 100 player in a bigger role, which beats his Yahoo rank of 116. No category is flagged weak, so he fits any build, and he adds threes, blocks and low turnovers. Early in the season, check his usage, whether his blocks stay near 1.6 rather than falling back to about 1.0, and whether his FG% climbs back from 42% toward 44 to 45%.
